days.module: LM4 The Time Value of Money in Finance
days.title: Compounding: how money grows
days.concept: Money invested at rate r for N periods grows to FV_N = PV(1 + r)^N because every period's interest itself earns interest.

memorize.front: Future value of a single sum (CFA notation)
memorize.back: FV_N = PV × (1 + r)^N

memorize.front: Simple interest earned over N periods
memorize.back: Interest = PV × r × N (no interest on interest)

memorize.front: Calculators allowed in the CFA exam room
memorize.back: Only the TI BA II Plus (incl. BA II Plus Professional) and the HP 12C family (incl. 12C Platinum); the TI-84 is not allowed, and results earned with it are voided
2ND P/Y 1 ENTER 2ND QUIT; 2ND FORMAT 4 ENTER, ↓ to Chn/AOS, 2ND SET until AOS, 2ND QUIT
Cash paid out is negative, cash received is positive; solving for I/Y or N needs a sign change among PV, PMT and FV (else BA II Plus Error 5 / TI-84 ERR:NO SIGN CHNG)

days.module: LM4 The Time Value of Money in Finance
days.title: Discounting: present value and implied rate
days.concept: Present value PV = FV_N / (1 + r)^N is compounding run backwards, and the same equation solves for the rate r = (FV/PV)^(1/N) − 1 or the number of periods N = ln(FV/PV)/ln(1 + r).

memorize.front: Present value of a single sum
memorize.back: PV = FV_N / (1 + r)^N

memorize.front: Discount factor for N periods at rate r
Implied rate from PV, FV and N
Number of periods from PV, FV and r
memorize.back: N = ln(FV_N / PV) / ln(1 + r)
Years to double ≈ 72 / (interest rate in percent) — a mental check, not a CFA formula

days.module: LM1 Returns of Financial Assets and Instruments
days.title: Required returns: real, nominal, after-tax
days.concept: A nominal required return is the real risk-free rate plus premiums for expected inflation, default, liquidity and maturity, and real and nominal rates are linked exactly by (1 + nominal) = (1 + real)(1 + inflation).

memorize.front: Components of a required interest rate
memorize.back: r = real risk-free rate + inflation premium + default risk premium + liquidity premium + maturity premium

memorize.front: Exact link between nominal and real rates
memorize.back: (1 + nominal rate) = (1 + real rate) × (1 + inflation rate)

memorize.front: Real rate from nominal and inflation (exact)
memorize.back: real = (1 + nominal) / (1 + inflation) − 1
nominal rf ≈ real rf + expected inflation
after-tax return = pre-tax return × (1 − tax rate)
Gross return: before management, custody and other administrative fees (trading costs already deducted); net return: after those fees

days.module: LM4 The Time Value of Money in Finance
days.title: Stated, effective and continuous rates
days.concept: Compounding m times a year turns a stated annual rate r_s into a larger effective annual rate EAR = (1 + r_s/m)^m − 1, which rises toward e^(r_s) − 1 as compounding becomes continuous.

memorize.front: Effective annual rate from a stated annual rate compounded m times
memorize.back: EAR = (1 + r_s/m)^m − 1

memorize.front: Future value with m compounding periods per year
memorize.back: FV_N = PV × (1 + r_s/m)^(m × N)
FV_N = PV × e^(r_s × N)
EAR = e^(r_s) − 1

memorize.front: Continuously compounded rate from an EAR (or holding-period growth)
memorize.back: r_cc = ln(1 + EAR)

memorize.front: Stated annual rate from an EAR (m compounding periods)

days.module: LM4 The Time Value of Money in Finance
days.title: Ordinary annuities: level payments
days.concept: A level payment A at the end of each of N periods is worth PV = A[1 − (1 + r)^−N]/r today and FV = A[(1 + r)^N − 1]/r at the end, because it is just N single sums discounted or compounded and added.

memorize.front: PV of an ordinary annuity of A per period for N periods at r

memorize.back: Payments at the END of each period; first payment at t = 1 (calculator END mode)
N = years × 12; periodic rate = annual stated rate / 12

days.module: LM4 The Time Value of Money in Finance
days.title: Annuity due: payments in advance
days.concept: When each payment comes at the start of the period, every payment is discounted one period less than in an ordinary annuity, so PV_due = PV_ordinary × (1 + r) and FV_due = FV_ordinary × (1 + r).

memorize.front: Annuity due as a split stream
memorize.back: PV_due = A + PV of an ordinary annuity of N − 1 payments

memorize.front: BA II Plus: switch to annuity-due mode
memorize.back: 2ND BGN 2ND SET 2ND QUIT (shows BGN); repeat to return to END
No — clearing TVM leaves BGN/END and P/Y unchanged

days.module: Review
days.title: Week 1 review: growth and discounting
days.concept: Review of Days 1–6: compounding and discounting single sums, required and real returns, effective and continuous rates, ordinary annuities and annuities due.

days.module: LM4 The Time Value of Money in Finance
days.title: Perpetuities: payments forever
days.concept: A level payment A received every period forever, starting one period from now, is worth PV = A/r, because the infinite sum of discounted payments converges; a perpetuity that starts later is valued at t − 1 and discounted back as a single sum.

memorize.front: PV of a level perpetuity, first payment one period from now
memorize.back: PV = A / r
r = A / PV

memorize.front: PV of a perpetuity whose first payment is at time t

memorize.back: PV = A_1 / (r − g), valid only if r > g
Cap rate = NOI / property value, so value = NOI / cap rate (a perpetuity with A = NOI)

days.module: LM4 The Time Value of Money in Finance
days.title: Amortizing loans: where each payment goes
days.concept: Each level loan payment first covers interest on the balance outstanding and only the remainder repays principal, so early payments are mostly interest and the balance at any time is the PV of the remaining payments.

memorize.front: Level payment on an amortizing loan

memorize.back: Interest_t = r × Balance_(t−1)
Principal_t = A − Interest_t
Balance_k = PV of the remaining N − k payments at the loan rate
Solve the loan in TVM first, then 2ND AMORT: P1, P2, ↓ BAL, ↓ PRN, ↓ INT

days.module: LM4 The Time Value of Money in Finance
days.title: Uneven cash flows: NPV and IRR
days.concept: An uneven stream is valued by discounting each cash flow separately and adding (cash-flow additivity), and its internal rate of return is the single discount rate that makes that net present value zero.

memorize.back: NPV = Σ_(t=0..N) CF_t / (1 + r)^t
IRR is the r that makes Σ CF_t / (1 + IRR)^t = 0
PVs of cash flows measured at the same point in time can be added
npv(rate in %, CF0, {CF1, CF2, …}[, {freq1, freq2, …}]); irr(CF0, {CF1, CF2, …}[, {freqs}]) returns a percent
CF 2ND CLR WORK; CFo ENTER ↓ C01 ENTER ↓ F01 ENTER ↓ …; NPV I ENTER ↓ CPT; IRR CPT

days.module: LM1 Returns of Financial Assets and Instruments (annualizing: LM2 Types of Financial Returns)
days.title: Holding-period returns and chain-linking
days.concept: Returns over successive periods compound by multiplying growth factors, (1 + R_1)(1 + R_2)…(1 + R_n) − 1, which is why a 50% loss needs a 100% gain to recover and why a period return is annualized as (1 + R_period)^c − 1.

memorize.front: Annualizing a return earned over a period (c periods per year)
memorize.back: R_annual = (1 + R_period)^c − 1 (for a return over several years, c = 1/years)

memorize.front: Gain needed to recover a loss L
memorize.back: Required gain = L / (1 − L) (a 50% loss needs +100%)

days.module: LM2 Types of Financial Returns
days.title: Arithmetic, geometric and harmonic means
days.concept: The arithmetic mean answers 'what is a typical one-period return', the geometric mean answers 'what constant return gives the same ending wealth', and the harmonic mean gives the average cost per share when the same amount of money is invested each period.

memorize.back: X̄_H = n / Σ(1 / X_i) (average cost per share when equal money is invested each period)

memorize.front: Order of the three means (positive values, not all equal)
memorize.back: harmonic < geometric < arithmetic

memorize.front: Approximate link between geometric and arithmetic means
memorize.back: R_G ≈ R̄ − σ²/2 (rough; poor when swings are large)

days.module: LM3 Benchmarking Returns
days.title: Money-weighted vs time-weighted returns
days.concept: The money-weighted return is the IRR of the investor's own cash flows and so rewards or punishes the timing of deposits and withdrawals, while the time-weighted return chain-links sub-period returns and so measures the manager regardless of those flows.

memorize.back: The IRR of the investor's cash flows: Σ CF_t / (1 + MWR)^t = 0
TWR = (1 + HPR_1)(1 + HPR_2)…(1 + HPR_n) − 1, annualized geometrically

memorize.front: When is TWR the right measure?
memorize.back: When the manager does not control the timing of external cash flows (manager evaluation)
MWR > TWR if more money is invested just before strong returns; MWR < TWR if before weak returns

days.module: Review
days.title: Week 2 review: streams of cash and returns
days.concept: Review of Days 8–13: perpetuities, amortization, NPV and IRR, holding-period and chain-linked returns, the three means, money- vs time-weighted returns.

days.module: Fixed-Income Bond Valuation: Prices and Yields
days.title: Pricing a bond from its yield
days.concept: A bond's price is the PV of its coupons (an annuity) plus the PV of its principal (a single sum), all discounted at the market yield, so the price falls when the yield rises and sits above par when the coupon rate exceeds the yield.

memorize.back: PV = FV / (1 + r)^N
PMT = annual coupon/2, rate = annual yield/2, N = 2 × years
Coupon rate > yield → premium; coupon rate < yield → discount; equal → par

days.module: Yield and Yield Spread Measures for Fixed-Rate Bonds
days.title: Yield to maturity, call and worst
days.concept: The yield to maturity is the IRR of buying a bond at its price and holding it to maturity; current yield, yield-to-call and yield-to-worst answer narrower questions, and yields can be compared only after converting them to the same periodicity.

memorize.back: Current yield = annual coupon / flat price
N = periods to the call date, FV = call price, PV = price, PMT = coupon; solve for r
The lowest of the YTM and the yields to every call date
(1 + APR_m/m)^m = (1 + APR_n/n)^n; semiannual-bond basis → annual-pay: (1 + r_s/2)^2 = 1 + r_annual
Held to maturity; all coupons and principal paid on time; coupons reinvested at the YTM
Simple yield = (annual coupon + straight-line amortized gain, or − amortized loss, per year) / flat price

days.module: Fixed-Income Bond Valuation: Prices and Yields
days.title: Full price, flat price and accrued interest
days.concept: Between coupon dates a buyer pays the full price — the bond's PV at the last coupon date moved forward to settlement, PV × (1 + r)^(t/T) — which splits into accrued interest owed to the seller for the days since the last coupon and the quoted flat price.

memorize.front: Full price of a bond between coupon dates
memorize.back: PV_full = PV_last coupon date × (1 + r)^(t/T)
AI = (t / T) × PMT (t = days since last coupon, T = days in the coupon period)
PV_flat = PV_full − AI
Government bonds: actual/actual; corporate bonds: 30/360

memorize.front: BA II Plus BOND worksheet output
memorize.back: PRI = flat price per 100 of par; full price = PRI + AI

days.module: Yield and Yield Spread Measures for Floating-Rate Instruments (repos: Fixed-Income Markets for Corporate Issuers)
days.title: Money-market yields and repos
days.concept: Money-market rates are quoted on a discount basis (on face value) or an add-on basis (on price) over 360- or 365-day years, so they must be converted to a common basis such as the 365-day add-on bond-equivalent yield before they are compared.

memorize.front: Price of a money-market instrument quoted on a discount basis
memorize.back: PV = FV × [1 − (Days/Year) × DR]
PV = FV / [1 + (Days/Year) × AOR]
AOR = (Year / Days) × (FV − PV) / PV
A 365-day add-on rate: BEY = (365 / Days) × (FV − PV) / PV
Repo interest = principal × repo rate × (days / 360)
Haircut = 1 − loan / collateral value, so loan = collateral value × (1 − haircut)

days.module: Equity Valuation: Concepts and Basic Tools
days.title: Constant-growth dividend discount model
days.concept: If dividends grow at a constant rate g forever, a share is a growing perpetuity worth V_0 = D_1/(r − g), and the same equation read backwards gives the market's implied required return r = D_1/P_0 + g or implied growth g = r − D_1/P_0.

memorize.front: Value of a non-callable, non-convertible preferred share
memorize.back: V_0 = D_p / r_p
Declaration date → ex-dividend date (shares bought on or after it do not get the dividend; price falls by about D) → holder-of-record date → payment date

memorize.front: Implied growth when only D_0 and P_0 are known

days.module: Equity Valuation: Concepts and Basic Tools
days.title: Two-stage dividend discount model
days.concept: When dividends grow fast for a few years and then settle into stable growth, value = PV of the explicit dividends + PV of a Gordon terminal value V_n = D_(n+1)/(r − g_L) placed at the start of stable growth.

memorize.front: Terminal value at the end of the high-growth stage
How many periods to discount the terminal value V_n
memorize.back: n periods (it is a value at time n)

days.module: Review
days.title: Week 3 review: bonds and dividend models
days.concept: Review of Days 15–20: bond prices from yields, yield measures and periodicity, full/flat price and accrued interest, money-market yields, constant-growth and two-stage dividend models.

days.module: LM3 Benchmarking Returns
days.title: Index weighting: price, value, equal
days.concept: An index's value and return depend on how it weights its members: a price-weighted index moves with share prices, so a stock split shrinks a company's influence and forces a new divisor, while a market-cap (value) index moves with company values and ignores splits.

memorize.back: Index = Σ P_i / divisor
Choose D_new so that Σ (post-split prices) / D_new = index value just before the split
w_i = (P_i × Q_i) / Σ (P_j × Q_j); float-adjusted uses float shares for Q
w_i = 1/N (must be rebalanced as prices move)

memorize.front: Index total return vs price return
memorize.back: Total return = price return + income (dividends) return
Shares outstanding − closely held shares (insiders, controlling owners, governments); float-adjusted weights use float shares

days.module: LM5 Statistical Characteristics of Asset Returns
days.title: Median, quantiles and trimmed means
days.concept: The median, quantiles and trimmed or winsorized means describe where returns sit without being dragged around by a few extreme values; the y-th percentile is found at position L_y = (n + 1)y/100 in the sorted data, interpolating between neighbours.

memorize.front: Location of the y-th percentile in n sorted observations
Interpolating a percentile at a non-integer location
memorize.back: P = X_(below) + (L_y − whole part) × (X_(above) − X_(below))
Discard a stated % of the lowest and highest observations, then average the rest (a 5% trimmed mean drops the lowest 2.5% and the highest 2.5%)
Replace the extreme observations with the nearest retained values, then average (a 95% winsorized mean resets the bottom and top 2.5%)
IQR = Q3 − Q1

days.module: LM5 Statistical Characteristics of Asset Returns
days.title: Dispersion: variance, SD and downside risk
days.concept: Variance and standard deviation measure how far returns typically stray from their mean (the sample version divides by n − 1), the coefficient of variation scales that risk per unit of mean return, and target downside deviation counts only the shortfalls below a chosen target.

memorize.back: s² = Σ (X_i − X̄)² / (n − 1)
σ² = Σ (X_i − μ)² / N
MAD = Σ |X_i − X̄| / n
CV = s / X̄ (risk per unit of mean return)
s_Target = √[ Σ_(X_i ≤ B) (X_i − B)² / (n − 1) ] — sum over observations at or below the target B, divide by n − 1 using all n

days.module: LM5 Statistical Characteristics of Asset Returns
days.title: Covariance and correlation
days.concept: Covariance measures whether two return series move together, and correlation rescales it to lie between −1 and +1 (r = s_XY/(s_X s_Y)) so that the strength of the co-movement can be compared across pairs.

memorize.back: s_XY = Σ (X_i − X̄)(Y_i − Ȳ) / (n − 1)
r_XY = s_XY / (s_X × s_Y)

memorize.front: Covariance from correlation (BA II Plus route)
memorize.back: s_XY = r × s_X × s_Y
−1 ≤ r ≤ +1; 0 means no LINEAR relation, not no relation
r_s = 1 − 6 Σ d_i² / [n (n² − 1)], d_i = difference between the two ranks of observation i

days.module: LM6 Statistical Distributions for Financial Asset Prices and Returns
days.title: Expected value and total probability
days.concept: An expected value weights each outcome by its probability, E(X) = Σ P(X_i)X_i, and when outcomes depend on which scenario occurs, the total probability rule averages the conditional expectations: E(X) = Σ E(X | S_i)P(S_i).

memorize.front: Expected value of a discrete random variable
memorize.back: E(X) = Σ P(X_i) × X_i

memorize.front: Variance of a discrete random variable
memorize.back: σ²(X) = Σ P(X_i) × [X_i − E(X)]²

memorize.front: Total probability rule for expected value
memorize.back: E(X) = E(X | S_1)P(S_1) + E(X | S_2)P(S_2) + … for mutually exclusive, exhaustive scenarios
P(AB) = P(A | B) × P(B)
P(A or B) = P(A) + P(B) − P(AB)
P(A | B) = P(A), so P(AB) = P(A) × P(B) — only then may probabilities simply be multiplied

days.module: LM6 Statistical Distributions for Financial Asset Prices and Returns
days.title: Bayes' formula: updating on evidence
days.concept: Bayes' formula updates a prior probability with new information, P(Event | Info) = [P(Info | Event)/P(Info)] × P(Event), where the unconditional P(Info) comes from the total probability rule over every way the information can arise.

memorize.back: P(Event | Information) = [P(Information | Event) / P(Information)] × P(Event)
P(I) = P(I | E)P(E) + P(I | not E)P(not E)
Prior = P(Event) before the information; posterior = P(Event | Information) after it
P(Information | Event) is not P(Event | Information); Bayes converts one into the other using the prior and P(Information)

days.module: Review
days.title: Week 4 review: indexes and statistics
days.concept: Review of Days 22–27: index weighting, location (median, quantiles, trimmed means), dispersion and downside deviation, covariance and correlation, expected value and the total probability rule, Bayes' formula.

days.module: LM6 Statistical Distributions for Financial Asset Prices and Returns
days.title: Binomial probabilities and counting
days.concept: With n independent trials each succeeding with probability p, the probability of exactly x successes is nCx p^x (1 − p)^(n − x), where nCx = n!/[(n − x)! x!] counts the ways the successes can be arranged.

memorize.front: Binomial probability of exactly x successes in n trials
memorize.back: P(X = x) = nCx × p^x × (1 − p)^(n − x)

memorize.front: Mean and variance of a binomial random variable
memorize.back: E(X) = n p; Var(X) = n p (1 − p)
nPr = n! / (n − r)!

days.module: LM6 Statistical Distributions for Financial Asset Prices and Returns
days.title: The normal curve and fat tails
days.concept: In a normal distribution the probability of an outcome depends only on how many standard deviations it lies from the mean, z = (X − μ)/σ, while real returns' skewness and excess kurtosis make extreme moves far more likely than the normal curve says.

memorize.back: z = (X − μ) / σ
Positive skew (long right tail): mean > median > mode; negative skew (long left tail): mean < median < mode
Excess kurtosis = sample kurtosis − 3; > 0 (leptokurtic) means fatter tails than the normal
The minimum loss expected over a period a given small % of the time (e.g. on the worst 5% of days): a left-tail percentile of returns

days.module: LM9 Simulation of Financial Asset Prices and Returns
days.title: Lognormal prices and Monte Carlo simulation
days.concept: If continuously compounded returns are normal, prices are lognormal — never negative and skewed right — and Monte Carlo simulation draws many random returns from such a model to build the whole distribution of outcomes when no formula is handy.

memorize.front: Continuously compounded return over a period
memorize.back: r_cc = ln(P_1 / P_0) = ln(1 + HPR)

memorize.front: Price from a continuously compounded return

memorize.back: If ln(P_T) is normal, P_T is lognormal: bounded below by 0 and skewed right
Draw random samples WITH replacement from the observed data to simulate the sampling distribution

days.module: LM8 The Return and Risk of a Financial Portfolio
days.title: Two-asset portfolio return and risk
days.concept: A portfolio's expected return is the weighted average of its assets' expected returns, but its variance also depends on how the assets move together: σ_p² = w_1²σ_1² + w_2²σ_2² + 2w_1w_2ρ_12σ_1σ_2.

memorize.back: E(R_p) = Σ w_i × E(R_i)
σ_p² = w_1²σ_1² + w_2²σ_2² + 2 w_1 w_2 ρ_12 σ_1 σ_2

memorize.front: Covariance from a joint probability table
memorize.back: Cov(R_A, R_B) = Σ P(R_A,i, R_B,j) × [R_A,i − E(R_A)] × [R_B,j − E(R_B)]

days.module: LM8 The Return and Risk of a Financial Portfolio
days.title: Minimum-variance portfolio and efficient frontier
days.concept: The lower the correlation, the bigger the diversification benefit: the two-asset weight that minimizes variance is w_1 = (σ_2² − Cov_12)/(σ_1² + σ_2² − 2Cov_12), and the efficient frontier is the upper part of the minimum-variance frontier, above the global minimum-variance portfolio.

memorize.back: The part of the minimum-variance frontier above (higher return than) the global minimum-variance portfolio
Whenever ρ < +1; the lower ρ, the larger the reduction

days.module: LM8 The Return and Risk of a Financial Portfolio
days.title: Risk aversion, utility and the capital allocation line
days.concept: A risk-averse investor scores a portfolio by utility U = E(r) − ½Aσ², and mixing the risk-free asset with the best risky portfolio gives a straight capital allocation line on which the highest-utility point depends on A; when the risky portfolio is the market, that line is the capital market line.

memorize.back: U = E(r) − ½ × A × σ² (decimals)

memorize.front: Capital allocation line (and CML with the market portfolio)
memorize.back: E(R_p) = R_f + [(E(R_i) − R_f) / σ_i] × σ_p

memorize.front: Optimal weight in the risky portfolio
memorize.back: w* = [E(R_i) − R_f] / (A × σ_i²)
SFRatio = [E(R_p) − R_L] / σ_p; choose the portfolio with the highest ratio

days.module: Review
days.title: Week 5 review: probability to portfolios
days.concept: Review of Days 29–34: binomial and counting, the normal curve, skewness and kurtosis, lognormal prices and simulation, two-asset portfolio risk, the minimum-variance portfolio and efficient frontier, utility and the capital allocation line.

days.module: The Term Structure of Interest Rates: Spot, Par, and Forward Curves
days.title: Spot rates and bootstrapping
days.concept: Each cash flow should be discounted at the zero-coupon (spot) rate for its own date, and spot rates can be bootstrapped one maturity at a time from the yields of par bonds.

memorize.back: PV = Σ CF_t / (1 + Z_t)^t (each cash flow at its own spot rate)

memorize.front: Discount factor from a spot rate
Bootstrapping step for an N-year par bond with coupon c (per 100)
memorize.back: 100 = c × DF_1 + … + c × DF_(N−1) + (100 + c) × DF_N → solve DF_N, then Z_N = DF_N^(−1/N) − 1

days.module: The Term Structure of Interest Rates: Spot, Par, and Forward Curves
days.title: Forward rates and par rates
days.concept: An implied forward rate is the future one-period rate that makes investing for two periods equal to investing for one and rolling over — (1 + Z_2)² = (1 + Z_1)(1 + IFR_(1,1)) — and the par rate is the coupon that prices a bond at par given the spot curve.

memorize.front: Implied forward rate between years A and B
Par rate for N years from discount factors
memorize.back: Par rate = (1 − DF_N) / (DF_1 + DF_2 + … + DF_N)

memorize.front: Spot and forward curves when the spot curve is inverted
memorize.back: Forward rates lie below spot rates

days.module: Yield and Yield Spread Measures for Fixed-Rate Bonds
days.title: Yield spreads and matrix pricing
days.concept: A yield spread is the extra yield over a benchmark — the G-spread over a government bond, the I-spread over swaps, the Z-spread added to every spot rate — and matrix pricing borrows the yields of comparable bonds to price one that rarely trades.

memorize.back: G-spread = YTM of the bond − YTM of the (interpolated) government bond of the same maturity
The constant Z that makes PV = Σ CF_t / (1 + z_t + Z)^t equal the bond's price
OAS = Z-spread − option value (in bps): callable OAS < Z-spread
y = y_short + (T − T_short)/(T_long − T_short) × (y_long − y_short)
Coupon = (MRR + quoted margin)/m × 100; discount rate = (MRR + discount margin)/m

days.module: Yield-Based Bond Duration Measures and Properties
days.title: Macaulay and modified duration
days.concept: Macaulay duration is the PV-weighted average time to a bond's cash flows, and modified duration = MacDur/(1 + r) turns it into the approximate percentage price fall for a 1-percentage-point rise in yield; MacDur is also the horizon at which price and reinvestment risk offset.

memorize.back: MacDur = Σ t × [CF_t/(1 + r)^t] / PV
ModDur = MacDur / (1 + r)
%ΔPV ≈ −AnnModDur × ΔYield
Duration gap = Macaulay duration − investment horizon

memorize.front: Macaulay duration of a zero-coupon bond
memorize.back: Equal to its time to maturity

days.module: Yield-Based Bond Duration Measures and Properties
days.title: Approximate duration, money duration and PVBP
days.concept: Price sensitivity can be measured by repricing the bond at yields a little higher and lower — ApproxModDur = (PV_− − PV_+)/(2 × ΔYield × PV_0) — and money duration and the price value of a basis point turn that sensitivity into currency.

memorize.back: ApproxModDur = (PV_− − PV_+) / (2 × ΔYield × PV_0)
MoneyDur = AnnModDur × PV_full (for the position)

memorize.front: Price value of a basis point
memorize.back: PVBP = (PV_− − PV_+) / 2, with yields ±1 bp
D_p ≈ Σ w_i × D_i, w_i = market-value weights

days.module: Yield-Based Bond Convexity and Portfolio Properties
days.title: Convexity: correcting the duration estimate
days.concept: Duration draws a straight line through a curved price–yield relation; adding ½ × convexity × (ΔYield)² corrects the estimate, so with positive convexity gains are larger and losses smaller than duration alone predicts — and the error grows with the size of the yield move.

memorize.back: ApproxCon = (PV_− + PV_+ − 2 × PV_0) / [(ΔYield)² × PV_0]

memorize.front: Price change with duration and convexity
memorize.back: %ΔPV ≈ −AnnModDur × ΔYield + ½ × AnnConvexity × (ΔYield)²

memorize.front: Sign of the convexity adjustment for an option-free bond
memorize.back: Always positive (adds to the estimate for yield rises and falls)

days.module: Review
days.title: Week 6 review: the yield curve and rate risk
days.concept: Review of Days 36–41: spot rates and bootstrapping, forward and par rates, yield spreads and matrix pricing, Macaulay and modified duration, approximate and money duration, PVBP, convexity.

days.module: LM7 Estimation and Hypothesis Testing
days.title: Standard error and confidence intervals
days.concept: By the central limit theorem the sample mean is approximately normal with standard error σ/√n, so a confidence interval is the point estimate ± reliability factor × standard error, using a t reliability factor with n − 1 degrees of freedom when σ is unknown.

memorize.front: Standard error of the sample mean
memorize.back: s_X̄ = s / √n (σ/√n if σ known)
X̄ ± (reliability factor) × standard error
Population variance unknown (use s); df = n − 1
For n ≥ 30, the sample mean is approximately normal with mean μ and variance σ²/n, whatever the population's distribution

days.module: LM7 Estimation and Hypothesis Testing
days.title: Hypothesis tests: testing a mean
days.concept: A hypothesis test asks whether a sample result is too far from the null hypothesis to be chance: compute test statistic = (sample statistic − hypothesized value)/standard error, compare it with the critical value or read its p-value, and know the two ways the decision can be wrong.

memorize.back: Rejecting a true null hypothesis; P(Type I) = α (significance level)
Type II = failing to reject a false null (probability β); power = 1 − β
Reject H_0 if p-value < α
'Fail to reject H_0' — never 'accept H_0'

days.module: LM7 Estimation and Hypothesis Testing
days.title: Comparing two means: pooled and paired
days.concept: To compare two groups, test the difference in means with a pooled-variance t-statistic when the samples are independent, but test the mean of the differences when observations come in matched pairs.

memorize.front: t-test for a difference in means (independent samples, equal variances)

memorize.back: t = d̄ / (s_d / √n), df = n − 1

memorize.front: Which test for matched data (same months, same firms)?
memorize.back: The paired-comparisons test (samples are dependent)

days.module: LM7 Estimation and Hypothesis Testing
days.title: Chi-square and F tests
days.concept: To test whether a variance equals a value use χ² = (n − 1)s²/σ_0² with n − 1 df, to compare two variances use F = s_1²/s_2² with the larger variance on top, and when the data are counts in categories a χ² test of independence compares observed with expected counts.

memorize.front: Chi-square test of a single variance
memorize.back: χ² = (n − 1) s² / σ_0², df = n − 1
F = s_1² / s_2² (larger sample variance on top), df = n_1 − 1 and n_2 − 1

memorize.front: Expected count in a contingency table
memorize.back: E_ij = (row i total × column j total) / overall total
χ² = Σ (O_ij − E_ij)² / E_ij, df = (r − 1)(c − 1)

days.module: LM10 Applications of Simple Linear Regression in Finance
days.title: Least squares: fitting the line
days.concept: Least squares fits the line Ŷ = b̂_0 + b̂_1X that minimizes the sum of squared vertical errors, which gives slope b̂_1 = Cov(X, Y)/Var(X) and intercept b̂_0 = Ȳ − b̂_1X̄.

memorize.back: b̂_1 = Cov(X, Y) / Var(X) = Σ(X_i − X̄)(Y_i − Ȳ) / Σ(X_i − X̄)²
e_i = Y_i − Ŷ_i = Y_i − (b̂_0 + b̂_1 X_i)

memorize.front: Four assumptions of simple linear regression
memorize.back: Linearity; homoskedasticity (constant error variance); independence of errors; normally distributed errors

memorize.front: BA II Plus LIN output names
memorize.back: a = intercept b̂_0; b = slope b̂_1; r = correlation

days.module: LM10 Applications of Simple Linear Regression in Finance
days.title: ANOVA, R² and the standard error
days.concept: Total variation in Y splits into an explained part and an unexplained part, SST = SSR + SSE; R² = SSR/SST measures the fit, the standard error of estimate √(SSE/(n − 2)) measures the typical miss, and F = MSR/MSE tests whether the slope explains anything at all.

memorize.back: SST = SSR + SSE
R² = SSR / SST (= r² with one independent variable)
MSE = SSE / (n − 2)
SEE = √MSE = √[SSE / (n − 2)]
F = MSR / MSE = (SSR / 1) / [SSE / (n − 2)], df = 1 and n − 2

days.module: Review
days.title: Week 7 review: inference and regression
days.concept: Review of Days 43–48: standard error and confidence intervals, testing a mean, pooled and paired tests, variance tests and non-parametric tests, least squares, ANOVA, R² and SEE.

days.module: LM10 Applications of Simple Linear Regression in Finance
days.title: Testing the slope; beta by regression
days.concept: The slope's t-statistic, (b̂_1 − B_1)/s_b̂1 with n − 2 df, tests whether X really moves Y; regressing a stock's returns on the market's gives its beta, and in simple regression the slope test is the same as the correlation test t = r√(n − 2)/√(1 − r²).

memorize.back: β = Cov(R_i, R_m) / Var(R_m) = slope of R_i regressed on R_m

memorize.front: Link between F and t in simple regression
memorize.back: F = t² (slope test)

days.module: LM10 Applications of Simple Linear Regression in Finance
days.title: Forecasts, prediction intervals and log models
days.concept: A regression forecast Ŷ_f = b̂_0 + b̂_1X_f comes with a prediction interval Ŷ_f ± t_c × s_f that widens as X_f moves away from X̄, and taking logs of Y and/or X lets a straight line fit exponential growth or elasticities.

memorize.back: s_f² = SEE² × [1 + 1/n + (X_f − X̄)² / ((n − 1) s_X²)]
Ŷ_f ± t_c × s_f, df = n − 2
ln Y = b_0 + b_1 X; forecast Y = e^(b_0 + b_1 X)
b_1 = elasticity: % change in Y for a 1% change in X

days.module: Portfolio Risk and Return: Part II
days.title: Beta, CAPM and the security market line
days.concept: Only systematic risk is rewarded, so an asset's expected return is E(R_i) = R_f + β_i[E(R_m) − R_f] with β_i = Cov(R_i, R_m)/σ_m² = ρ_im σ_i/σ_m; an asset that plots above the security market line is undervalued (positive alpha).

memorize.back: β_i = Cov(R_i, R_m) / σ_m² = ρ_im × σ_i / σ_m
E(R_i) = R_f + β_i × [E(R_m) − R_f]
α = forecast (or actual) return − CAPM required return; α > 0 → undervalued
E(R_p) = R_F + λ_1 β_p,1 + … + λ_K β_p,K
CML: total risk σ (efficient portfolios); SML: beta (any asset or portfolio)

days.module: Portfolio Risk and Return: Part II
days.title: Risk-adjusted performance measures
days.concept: Risk-adjusted measures compare excess return with the risk that matters: the Sharpe ratio uses total risk σ, Treynor and Jensen's alpha use beta, M² restates the Sharpe ratio as a return at the market's risk, and Sortino and Calmar look at downside risk and drawdowns.

memorize.back: Sharpe = (R_p − R_f) / σ_p
Treynor = (R_p − R_f) / β_p
M² = (R_p − R_f) × (σ_m / σ_p) − (R_m − R_f); equivalently, the risk-adjusted return R_f + (R_p − R_f) × σ_m/σ_p compared with R_m
α_p = R_p − [R_f + β_p (R_m − R_f)]
Sortino = (R_p − MAR) / downside deviation

days.module: Curve-Based and Empirical Fixed-Income Risk Measures
days.title: Effective duration and negative convexity
days.concept: When cash flows change with interest rates — callable bonds and mortgage securities — sensitivity must be measured by repricing under shifts of the benchmark curve, EffDur = (PV_− − PV_+)/(2 × ΔCurve × PV_0), and prepayments give mortgage securities negative convexity.

memorize.back: EffDur = (PV_− − PV_+) / (2 × ΔCurve × PV_0)
EffCon = [PV_− + PV_+ − 2 × PV_0] / [(ΔCurve)² × PV_0]

memorize.front: Conditional prepayment rate from the single monthly mortality

memorize.back: Price rises less when rates fall than it falls when rates rise (callables, MBS)
Sum of key rate durations = effective duration

days.module: Credit Risk
days.title: Credit risk: expected loss and spreads
days.concept: Expected loss equals the probability of default times the loss given default (exposure × (1 − recovery rate)); the credit spread is roughly that annual expected loss, and a spread change moves a bond's price by about −ModDur × ΔSpread + ½ × Convexity × (ΔSpread)².

memorize.back: EL = probability of default × loss given default
LGD = exposure × (1 − recovery rate)
Spread ≈ POD × LGD (as % of exposure per year)

memorize.front: Price change from a spread change
memorize.back: %ΔPV ≈ −ModDur × ΔSpread + ½ × Convexity × (ΔSpread)²

memorize.front: Leverage ratios used by credit analysts
memorize.back: Debt/EBITDA, FFO/debt, debt/capital; coverage: EBITDA/interest

days.module: Review
days.title: Week 8 review: regression to credit
days.concept: Review of Days 50–55: slope tests and beta by regression, forecasts and log models, CAPM and the SML, risk-adjusted performance, effective duration and negative convexity, credit risk. Plus a one-paragraph note on Quantitative Methods LM11 Introduction to Financial Data Science (big data, machine learning, AI and LLMs — described only, no calculations).

days.module: Pricing and Valuation of Forward Contracts and for an Underlying with Varying Maturities
days.title: Forward prices and the cost of carry
days.concept: No-arbitrage forces a forward price to equal the spot price carried forward at the risk-free rate, adjusted for income forgone and costs paid — F_0(T) = [S_0 − PV(I) + PV(C)](1 + r)^T — and the forward's value later is the PV of the change in the forward price.

memorize.front: Forward price with income and costs
Value of a long forward at time t

memorize.back: Total return = price return + roll return + collateral return

days.module: Pricing and Valuation of Interest Rate and Other Swaps
days.title: FRAs and interest rate swaps
days.concept: A forward rate agreement locks in an implied forward rate, and an interest rate swap is a bundle of such forward agreements whose fixed rate is set so the PV of fixed payments equals the PV of floating ones: s_N = (1 − DF_N)/Σ DF_i.

memorize.front: Par swap rate from discount factors
FRA settlement amount (paid at the start of the period)
memorize.back: Notional × (MRR − FRA rate) × (days/360) / [1 + MRR × (days/360)]
The fixed-rate payer (floating receiver) in a swap; the long FRA

days.module: Pricing and Valuation of Options
days.title: Option payoffs, profits and value
days.concept: At expiry a call pays max(0, S_T − X) and a put max(0, X − S_T); profit subtracts the premium, so breakevens are X + c_0 for a call and X − p_0 for a put; before expiry an option's price is its intrinsic value plus time value, bounded below by no-arbitrage.

memorize.back: c_T = max(0, S_T − X)
p_T = max(0, X − S_T)
Long call: S_T = X + c_0; long put: S_T = X − p_0

memorize.front: Lower bound of a European call
Lower bound of a European put

days.module: Option Replication Using Put-Call Parity
days.title: Put-call parity and synthetic positions
days.concept: A call plus a risk-free bond paying the strike (a fiduciary call) has the same payoff as a put plus the stock (a protective put), so S_0 + p_0 = c_0 + X/(1 + r)^T, any one price follows from the others, and with a forward F_0/(1 + r)^T + p_0 = c_0 + X/(1 + r)^T.

days.module: Valuing a Derivative Using a One-Period Binomial Model
days.title: One-period binomial option pricing
days.concept: In a one-period binomial model an option is priced by building a riskless hedge of stock and option, which yields the risk-neutral probability π = (1 + r − d)/(u − d) and the option value c_0 = [π c_u + (1 − π) c_d]/(1 + r) — real-world probabilities never enter.

memorize.front: Risk-neutral probability of an up move

memorize.back: h = (c_u − c_d) / (S_u − S_d)
d < 1 + r < u

days.module: Exchange Rate Calculations
days.title: Exchange rates and cross rates
days.concept: An exchange rate A/B is the price of one unit of the base currency B in units of the price currency A, cross rates follow by multiplying quotes so the common currency cancels, and one currency's percentage change against another is not the negative of the other's.

memorize.back: Number of units of currency A (price) per 1 unit of currency B (base)
(A/B) × (B/C) = A/C

memorize.front: Percentage change of the base currency in an A/B quote
memorize.back: %Δ = (A/B)_new / (A/B)_old − 1

memorize.front: Percentage change of the price currency against the base
memorize.back: %Δ_price = 1 / (1 + %Δ_base) − 1

days.module: Review
days.title: Week 9 review: derivatives and currencies
days.concept: Review of Days 57–62: forward prices and value, FRAs and swaps, option payoffs and bounds, put-call parity, the one-period binomial model, exchange-rate quotes and cross rates.

days.module: Analysis of Inventories
days.title: Inventory: FIFO, LIFO and weighted average
days.concept: When unit costs change, the cost-flow assumption decides which costs land in cost of goods sold and which stay in ending inventory — FIFO expenses the oldest costs, LIFO the newest, weighted average the mean — so in rising prices LIFO reports higher COGS, lower profit and lower taxes.

memorize.back: Beginning inventory + purchases = COGS + ending inventory
Cost of goods available for sale / units available for sale

memorize.front: FIFO vs LIFO when prices are rising
memorize.back: LIFO: higher COGS, lower gross profit and taxes, lower ending inventory; FIFO: the reverse
US GAAP only; IFRS prohibits LIFO

memorize.front: Inventory turnover and days on hand
memorize.back: Turnover = COGS / average inventory; DOH = 365 / turnover

days.module: Analysis of Inventories
days.title: LIFO reserve, LIFO liquidation and NRV
days.concept: The LIFO reserve (FIFO inventory − LIFO inventory) lets an analyst restate a LIFO company as if it used FIFO — inventory + reserve, COGS − change in reserve, equity + reserve × (1 − t) — while a LIFO liquidation flatters profit with old, cheap costs and inventory is written down when it is worth less than cost.

memorize.back: Inventory_FIFO = Inventory_LIFO + LIFO reserve
COGS_FIFO = COGS_LIFO − ΔLIFO reserve

memorize.front: Equity adjustment when restating to FIFO
memorize.back: Equity increases by LIFO reserve × (1 − tax rate)
NRV = estimated selling price − estimated costs to complete and sell
Units sold exceed units purchased, so old low-cost layers enter COGS (LIFO reserve falls)

days.module: Analysis of Long-Term Assets
days.title: Capitalize or expense?
days.concept: Capitalizing a cost puts it on the balance sheet and spreads it over later years as depreciation, so it raises current profit, assets and equity and moves the cash outflow from operating to investing activities — and capitalized interest does the same with borrowing costs during construction.

memorize.front: Effect of capitalizing (vs expensing) in the first year
memorize.back: Higher net income, assets and equity; higher CFO and lower (more negative) CFI
Total expense and total cash flow are the same; capitalizing smooths expense into later years
Added to the asset's cost (later depreciated); cash paid classified in CFI
Interest coverage = EBIT / interest expense (analysts often add capitalized interest to the denominator)

days.module: Analysis of Long-Term Assets
days.title: Depreciation methods and asset age
days.concept: Depreciation spreads an asset's cost minus salvage over its life — straight-line evenly, double-declining-balance at 2/n of each year's opening book value (front-loaded, stopping at salvage), units-of-production by use — and ratios of the accounts reveal an asset base's age and remaining life.

memorize.back: (Cost − salvage value) / useful life
(2 / useful life) × beginning book value (salvage ignored until book value would fall below it)
(Cost − salvage) × (units this period / total expected units)
Accumulated depreciation / annual depreciation expense
Net PPE / annual depreciation expense

days.module: Analysis of Long-Term Assets
days.title: Impairment, revaluation and disposal
days.concept: When an asset's carrying amount exceeds what it can recover, it is written down — under IFRS to the recoverable amount (higher of fair value less costs to sell and value in use), under US GAAP to fair value after a recoverability test on undiscounted cash flows — and selling an asset books a gain or loss of proceeds minus carrying amount.

memorize.back: Higher of fair value less costs to sell and value in use
Impaired if carrying amount > undiscounted expected future cash flows; loss = carrying amount − fair value
IFRS: allowed (up to original carrying amount); US GAAP: not allowed for assets held for use
Gain (loss) = sale proceeds − carrying amount

days.module: Topics in Long-Term Liabilities and Equity
days.title: Leases on the balance sheet
days.concept: A lessee records a right-of-use asset and a lease liability equal to the PV of the lease payments, and the liability then amortizes like a loan: each period interest accrues on the balance and the payment reduces it.

memorize.back: PV of the lease payments discounted at the implicit rate (or the lessee's incremental borrowing rate)
Lease liability + initial direct costs + lease payments made at or before commencement − incentives
Depreciation of the ROU asset + interest on the lease liability
On the balance sheet; single straight-line lease cost in the income statement

days.module: Review
days.title: Week 10 review: inventories and long-lived assets
days.concept: Review of Days 64–69: FIFO, LIFO and weighted average; LIFO reserve and liquidation; NRV write-downs; capitalize vs expense; depreciation methods and asset age; impairment, revaluation and disposal; lessee lease accounting.

days.module: Analysis of Income Taxes
days.title: Deferred taxes: DTL and DTA
days.concept: Income tax expense differs from taxes payable because accounting and tax rules recognise items at different times: a deferred tax liability arises when an asset's carrying amount exceeds its tax base, DTL = (carrying amount − tax base) × t, and income tax expense = taxes payable + ΔDTL − ΔDTA.

memorize.front: Deferred tax liability on an asset
memorize.back: DTL = (carrying amount − tax base) × tax rate, when carrying amount > tax base

memorize.front: Deferred tax asset on an asset
memorize.back: DTA = (tax base − carrying amount) × tax rate, when tax base > carrying amount
Income tax expense = taxes payable + ΔDTL − ΔDTA
Differences that never reverse (e.g. tax-exempt income, non-deductible fines): no deferred tax; they change the effective rate

days.module: Analysis of Income Taxes
days.title: Tax rates, reconciliation and rate changes
days.concept: The effective tax rate (income tax expense/pre-tax income) differs from the statutory rate because of permanent differences, foreign rates and credits, the reconciliation explains each gap, and when the tax rate changes deferred tax assets and liabilities are remeasured with the change flowing through tax expense.

memorize.back: Effective tax rate = income tax expense / pre-tax income
Cash tax rate = cash taxes paid / pre-tax income

memorize.front: Effect of a tax-rate change on deferred taxes
memorize.back: Remeasure DTL and DTA at the new enacted rate; the change goes through income tax expense

memorize.front: Tax-rate cut with a net DTA
memorize.back: DTA falls in value → one-time increase in tax expense

days.module: Analyzing Income Statements
days.title: Basic and diluted EPS
days.concept: Basic EPS divides earnings available to common shareholders by the weighted-average shares outstanding; diluted EPS adds the extra shares that convertibles, options and warrants would create — and adds back what they cost — using the if-converted and treasury stock methods, and ignores anything antidilutive.

memorize.back: Basic EPS = (net income − preferred dividends) / weighted-average number of common shares
[NI − preferred dividends + convertible interest × (1 − t)] / (weighted-average shares + shares from conversion)
New shares = shares from exercise − (exercise proceeds / average market price)
Exclude any security whose inclusion would increase diluted EPS

memorize.front: When does a debt-funded share buyback raise EPS?
memorize.back: When the earnings yield E/P exceeds the after-tax cost of debt r_d × (1 − t)

days.module: Analyzing Statements of Cash Flows I
days.title: Cash from operations: indirect and direct
days.concept: Profit and cash differ: the indirect method starts with net income, adds back non-cash charges and losses, subtracts gains, and adjusts for working capital (an increase in an operating asset uses cash, an increase in an operating liability provides it), while the direct method rebuilds cash received and paid line by line.

memorize.back: CFO = NI + non-cash charges − gains + losses − increases in operating assets + increases in operating liabilities
Revenue − increase in accounts receivable
COGS + increase in inventory − increase in accounts payable
US GAAP: CFO; IFRS: CFO or CFF

days.module: Analyzing Statements of Cash Flows II
days.title: Free cash flow: FCFF and FCFE
days.concept: Free cash flow is what is left after the business funds its investment: free cash flow to the firm, FCFF = CFO + Int(1 − t) − FCInv, belongs to all capital providers, and free cash flow to equity, FCFE = CFO − FCInv + net borrowing, belongs to shareholders.

memorize.front: Free cash flow to the firm from CFO
memorize.back: FCFF = CFO + Int × (1 − t) − FCInv

memorize.front: Free cash flow to equity from CFO
memorize.back: FCFE = CFO − FCInv + net borrowing
FCFF = NI + NCC + Int × (1 − t) − FCInv − WCInv
(CFO + interest paid + taxes paid) / interest paid

days.module: Financial Analysis Techniques
days.title: Common-size, activity ratios and the CCC
days.concept: Dividing by sales turns statements into common-size percentages and balances into days — DSO, DOH and DPO — whose combination DOH + DSO − DPO, the cash conversion cycle, measures how long cash is tied up in operations, and a sales-based pro forma forecasts next year's statements from those same percentages and days.

memorize.back: DSO = 365 / (revenue / average receivables)
DOH = 365 / (COGS / average inventory)
DPO = 365 / (purchases / average payables)
CCC = DOH + DSO − DPO
Income statement: each item / revenue; balance sheet: each item / total assets
Receivables = DSO × forecast revenue / 365

days.module: Review
days.title: Week 11 review: taxes, EPS and cash flows
days.concept: Review of Days 71–76: deferred taxes, effective and cash tax rates and rate changes, basic and diluted EPS and buybacks, indirect and direct CFO, FCFF and FCFE, common-size statements, activity ratios, the cash conversion cycle and the sales-based pro forma.

days.module: Financial Analysis Techniques
days.title: DuPont: what drives ROE
days.concept: Return on equity can be split to show why it is high or low — ROE = (NI/EBT)(EBT/EBIT)(EBIT/Revenue)(Revenue/Average assets)(Average assets/Average equity) — separating tax burden, interest burden, operating margin, asset turnover and financial leverage, and solvency ratios measure the risk behind the last two factors.

memorize.back: ROE = (NI / revenue) × (revenue / average total assets) × (average total assets / average equity)
ROE = (NI/EBT) × (EBT/EBIT) × (EBIT/revenue) × (revenue/average assets) × (average assets/average equity)
Average total assets / average total equity
EBIT / interest payments
(EBIT + lease payments) / (interest payments + lease payments)
Total debt / (total debt + total shareholders' equity)

days.module: Equity Valuation: Concepts and Basic Tools
days.title: Sustainable growth and the justified P/E
days.concept: A firm that reinvests a fraction b of earnings at its return on equity can grow dividends at g = b × ROE, and putting that into the Gordon model gives the justified leading P/E = (1 − b)/(r − g), linking a fair multiple to payout, growth and risk.

memorize.back: g = b × ROE (b = retention ratio)
Payout = D / E = 1 − b

days.module: Equity Valuation: Concepts and Basic Tools
days.title: Multiples and enterprise value
days.concept: Multiples price a company relative to what it earns or owns, and EV/EBITDA uses enterprise value — equity value plus debt and preferred stock minus cash — so that companies with very different debt levels can be compared on their whole operating business.

memorize.back: EV = market value of equity + debt + preferred stock + non-controlling interest − cash and short-term investments
Enterprise value / EBITDA (compare firms with different capital structures)
P/B = market price per share / book value per share
RI_t = NI_t − r × B_(t−1)

days.module: Capital Investments and Capital Allocation
days.title: Capital budgeting: NPV, IRR and ROIC
days.concept: A company should accept a project when its NPV at the cost of capital is positive; the IRR agrees for a single conventional project but can mislead when ranking mutually exclusive projects of different size or timing, and sunk costs never enter the decision.

memorize.back: Accept if NPV > 0; for mutually exclusive projects choose the highest NPV
Accept if IRR > required rate of return (cost of capital)
ROIC = after-tax operating profit / average book value of invested capital
The discount rate at which two projects' NPVs are equal (the IRR of the differences in cash flows)
Never included in project cash flows

days.module: Capital Structure
days.title: The weighted average cost of capital
days.concept: The weighted average cost of capital blends the after-tax cost of debt, the cost of preferred stock and the cost of equity by target market-value weights, WACC = w_d r_d(1 − t) + w_p r_p + w_e r_e, and it is the hurdle rate for average-risk projects.

memorize.back: WACC = w_d × r_d × (1 − t) + w_p × r_p + w_e × r_e
r_d × (1 − t), with r_d = YTM of the firm's debt
r_p = D_p / P_p
r_e = R_f + β × [E(R_m) − R_f]
V_L = V_U + t × D (value rises with debt via the tax shield)

days.module: Exchange Rate Calculations
days.title: Forward exchange rates and interest parity
days.concept: A forward exchange rate is the spot rate adjusted for the two currencies' interest rates, F_(A/B) = S_(A/B) × [1 + i_A(days/360)]/[1 + i_B(days/360)] with A the price currency and B the base currency, so the higher-interest currency trades at a forward discount and a hedged carry trade earns nothing extra.

memorize.front: Covered interest rate parity (A/B quote, A = price currency, B = base currency)

memorize.back: F = S + points / 10,000 (÷ 100 when the quote has two decimals, e.g. JPY)

memorize.front: Which currency trades at a forward discount?
memorize.back: The currency with the higher interest rate
F − S > 0: the base currency trades at a forward premium

days.module: Review
days.title: Week 12 review: ratios, valuation and capital
days.concept: Review of Days 78–83: DuPont, profitability, solvency and coverage ratios, sustainable growth and the justified P/E, multiples and enterprise value, capital budgeting with NPV/IRR/ROIC, the WACC, forward exchange rates and covered interest parity.

days.module: Working Capital and Liquidity
days.title: Liquidity ratios and the cost of trade credit
days.concept: Liquidity ratios — current, quick, cash and the defensive interval — measure whether near-term obligations can be met, and skipping a supplier's early-payment discount is borrowing at cost = [1 + d/(1 − d)]^(365/days beyond the discount period) − 1, to be compared with other short-term funding.

memorize.back: Cost = [1 + discount / (1 − discount)]^(365 / days beyond the discount period) − 1
2% discount if paid within 10 days; otherwise the full amount is due in 30 days
Yes if the cost of trade credit exceeds the cost of alternative short-term financing
(Cash + short-term marketable investments + receivables) / current liabilities
(Cash + short-term marketable investments + receivables) / daily cash expenditures

days.module: Firms and Market Structures
days.title: Profit maximization, shutdown and concentration
days.concept: Every firm maximizes profit where marginal revenue equals marginal cost, breaks even where price equals average total cost, shuts down in the short run when price falls below average variable cost, and the Herfindahl-Hirschman Index (the sum of squared market shares) gauges how concentrated its market is.

memorize.back: Produce where MR = MC
Shut down if price < average variable cost; operate (even at a loss) if AVC ≤ P < ATC
P = ATC (economic profit = 0)
HHI = Σ (market share_i)², shares in percent (max 10,000)
Sum of the market shares of the N largest firms

days.module: Alternative Investment Performance and Returns
days.title: Hedge-fund fees: from gross to net
days.concept: Hedge-fund investors earn the gross return minus a management fee and an incentive fee on profits above any hurdle and high-water mark, so a '2 and 20' fund must earn a large gross return just to match an index fund, and a fund of funds adds a second layer of fees.

memorize.back: Net return = (ending NAV after all fees − beginning NAV) / beginning NAV

memorize.front: Incentive fee net of management fee, hard hurdle
memorize.back: Incentive = rate × max[0, ending assets − management fee − beginning assets × (1 + hurdle)]
Incentive fees are paid only on value above the highest previous NAV (net of fees)
R_L = R + (V_B / V_E) × (R − r_D)

days.module: Alternative Investment Performance and Returns
days.title: Private equity waterfalls, IRR and MOIC
days.concept: In private equity the distribution waterfall decides when the general partner earns carried interest — after investors have their capital and preferred return back, either across the whole fund (European) or deal by deal (American), with catch-up and clawback provisions — and performance is reported as IRR and the multiple of invested capital.

memorize.back: MOIC = (realized value + unrealized value) / total invested capital
LPs receive all contributed capital plus the preferred return before the GP earns carry
Carry is paid on each deal as it is exited (earlier for the GP; clawback risk for LPs)
After the preferred return, the GP receives (most or all of) distributions until it has its full carry share of total profits
GP must return carry received in excess of its entitled share over the life of the fund

days.module: Mock exam — session 1 topics
days.title: Mock exam 1: Quant, Economics, FSA
days.concept: CFA-style mock in the order of the real exam's first session (math topics only): 30 three-option questions in about 45 minutes (90 seconds each) on Quantitative Methods, Economics and Financial Statement Analysis, graded on the page, with a topic breakdown to show where to focus from February to May.

days.module: Mock exam — session 2 topics
days.title: Mock exam 2: FI, Equities, Derivatives and more
